questions.prompt: A browser app needs to clone a data graph containing a cycle and a Map without transferring anything. Which supported result can structuredClone produce?

choices.text: The same graph with nested aliases.
The same graph object with every nested object still shared with the source.
A clone only after every Map has been rewritten into enumerable properties.
An independent graph retaining the cycle and Map.

questions.explanation: Structured cloning supports cycles and Maps and creates a separate graph. It is not JSON serialization and does not retain ordinary nested object aliases to the source.

sources.title: HTML Standard
sources.claim: The structured clone algorithm preserves cycles and supported built-in data such as Map but rejects function objects with DataCloneError.

questions.prompt: An app calls structuredClone on an ArrayBuffer and includes that buffer in the transfer list. What happens to the original buffer?

choices.text: It becomes detached.
It stays readable on both sides.
It is converted to a SharedArrayBuffer so both sides may write freely.
It retains a private byte copy until the cloned buffer is garbage collected.

questions.explanation: ArrayBuffer transfer moves ownership of its data and detaches the original. Sharing or keeping an independent source copy would be different operations.

sources.title: HTML Standard
sources.claim: Transferring an ArrayBuffer moves its backing data and detaches the original buffer; transfer-list entries must be reachable in the serialized value to appear in the result.

questions.prompt: An async generator manages a resource in try/finally, and its consumer uses for await...of. Which behaviors are specified? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The loop awaits the result of an asynchronous return method.
A synchronous iterable can also be consumed by for await...of.
break discards the generator without running its finally cleanup.
Every iteration is launched concurrently before any yielded value is awaited.
Breaking from the loop invokes the iterator's return method when present.

questions.explanation: A is correct: AsyncIteratorClose awaits completion before the early exit finishes. B is correct: the language wraps its iterator using an async-from-sync adapter. C is incorrect: closing via return allows generator finally cleanup to execute. D is incorrect: for-await consumption processes the iterator steps sequentially. E is correct: early loop exit performs iterator closing.

sources.title: ECMAScript® 2027 Language Specification
sources.claim: for-await-of closes an iterator on early exit and awaits asynchronous iterator return completion; it consumes async iterables and wraps sync iterables.

sources.title: ECMAScript® 2027 Language Specification
sources.claim: The for-await-of evaluation closes the iterator on early exit and ends normally when the iterator reports done.

sources.title: ECMAScript® 2027 Language Specification
sources.claim: AsyncIteratorClose obtains the return method and awaits its result before completing the close.

questions.prompt: A plain data object passed to browser structuredClone has an own property whose value is a function. What should the caller expect?

choices.text: A successful function-and-closure clone.
A DataCloneError.
A successful clone that replaces the function with its executable source code.
An automatic transfer of the function into a dedicated browser worker first.

questions.explanation: Function objects are not serializable by the structured clone algorithm. It throws rather than copying code and closures or creating a worker.

sources.title: HTML Standard
sources.claim: The structured clone algorithm preserves cycles and supported built-in data such as Map but rejects function objects with DataCloneError.

questions.prompt: A browser clones an object without a transfer list, and the object contains an ArrayBuffer. Which ownership result applies?

choices.text: The original is detached automatically.
Both objects receive a shared backing store with atomic synchronization.
The buffer data is copied.
The buffer is omitted because ArrayBuffers can only be transferred, not cloned.

questions.explanation: ArrayBuffers can be cloned or transferred. Ordinary cloning copies the data; detachment requires transferring that buffer.

sources.title: HTML Standard
sources.claim: Transferring an ArrayBuffer moves its backing data and detaches the original buffer; transfer-list entries must be reachable in the serialized value to appear in the result.

questions.prompt: A custom async iterator supplies next and return methods. Which statements describe for await...of consumption? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An async return promise is always ignored during an early loop exit.
The construct automatically parallelizes the iterator's next calls.
An early return from the consuming function can trigger iterator closing.
Normal exhaustion does not require an extra return call.
A synchronous iterator is rejected solely because it lacks Symbol.asyncIterator.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: the closing algorithm awaits that result. B is incorrect: the loop awaits successive steps instead of requesting all steps concurrently. C is correct: abrupt completion leaving the loop closes the iterator. D is correct: the done result completes the loop without the early-exit close path. E is incorrect: for-await can obtain and wrap a synchronous iterator.
